title: A Junior Researcher in the field of Superconducting Quantum Devices at FBK
description:
Fondazione Bruno Kessler is a research institution devoted to excellence in research in numerous disciplines and designated to the role of keeping the Autonomous Province of Trento in the mainstream of European and international research. Each research area is assigned to a specific research centre, of which there are twelve totals. Information regarding the research centres, their activities, and scientific directions is available at http://www.fbk.eu/research-centers.
Workplace
The FBK Centre for Sensors and Devices (FBK-SD) is a research centre that operates in the following scientific and technological areas: materials and interfaces, devices and microsystems, integrated systems, quantum sensors and quantum technologies. FBK-SD has extremely advanced technical know-how in materials science, innovative device design and microfabrication technologies.
The SQD Research Unit focuses on the development of superconducting quantum devices, from design and microfabrication in the FBK cleanroom facility to cryogenic characterisation and final experiments in a dedicated cryogenic laboratory. Such devices include superconducting parametric amplifiers, qubits and cryogenic detectors, based on Josephson junctions and high kinetic inductance devices. The applications span from circuit Quantum Electrodynamics (cQED) and microwave quantum optics experiments to quantum sensing, particle physics, and space applications. FBK actively seeks diversity and inclusion in the workplace and is also committed to promoting gender equality. To promote the inclusion of disabled staff as per law 68/99, the Foundation is available and interested in evaluating the applications received for technical-scientific domains that do not correspond exactly to this call.

Job Description
The selected candidate will contribute to R&D activities for the microfabrication of superconducting quantum circuits, with specific responsibilities related to optimisation of microfabrication processes and fabrication of devices. The focus of the activities will be on Josephson junctions-based devices, such as Josephson Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifiers.
The successful candidate will contribute to the following tasks: Development and optimisation of lithographic processes (such as direct laser writing) for Josephson junctions; Development and optimisation of film deposition and etching processes for Josephson junctions-based devices; Execution of cleanroom processes for the complete microfabrication of Josephson junctions-based devices; Analysis of experimental data and interpretation of results to improve the device microfabrication flow; Contributing to the preparation of scientific publications and project reporting.
Job requirements
The ideal candidate should have: Master’s Degree in Physics, to be obtained by the start date of the contract; Good knowledge of the physics of superconducting circuits and Josephson effect; Experience in the R&D of superconducting quantum circuits; Experience in cleanroom processes and microfabrication R&D, also on 150mm wafer scale; Proficiency in Python coding and data analysis; Excellent English, written and spoken (At least B2); Strong sense of curiosity and willingness to learn and develop; Strong orientation to results, determination, flexibility and aptitude for problem-solving. Furthermore, the following elements will be positively evaluated: Specific experience in operating a direct laser writer system for high-resolution optical lithography; Specific experience in cleanroom processes for Al/AlOx/Al Josephson junctions; Specific experience in RF magnetron sputtering of thin films of superconducting metals; Specific experience in the design and microfabrication of Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifiers; Experience in RF cryogenic measurements with dilution refrigerations; Good understanding of modelling of superconducting circuits and in particular of Travelling Wave Parametric Amplifiers.

Gross annual salary: about € 41.200 plus objectives achievements bonus
Benefits: flexi-time, company subsidized cafeteria or meal vouchers, internal car park, welcome office support for visa formalities and for research in accommodation, etc., supplementary pension and health fund, social security (SANIFONDS), family-work balance, free training courses, support on bank account opening, discount on public transport, sport, language course fees, counseling and psychological support service. title: A position for a Developer in the area of Social Digital Twins at Digital Society Research Center
description:
Digital Society (DigiS) is a research center of Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) formed by a multidisciplinary team of more than 100 researchers, technologists, and managers (including Ph.D. and students). It is organized in 7 research units dedicated to specific research areas in the AI and ICT domain and two support units focusing on project management and technology maturation. Our mission is to perform advanced research and develop innovative digital technology to address the future digital society’s key challenges. Digital technology has a pervasive impact on our lives and is reshaping our society. The challenge is to ensure that digital technology becomes a steppingstone to create a more sustainable, inclusive, and secure society. More information is available at https://digis.fbk.eu/#vision.
The position is opened by the Modeling and Simulation of Socio-Technical Systems (MoST) research unit of the Digital Society center. The unit aims to research new modeling and simulation techniques for complex socio-technical systems (e.g., cities, rural areas, complex organizations) by exploiting, developing and integrating data science, artificial intelligence and complex systems approaches. One of the key research areas of the MoST unit are Social Digital Twins, namely dynamic digital models of socio-technical systems, fed by data collected from the systems themselves, and capable of faithfully reproducing their behavior and of predicting their evolution, including the effects and impacts of external changes (eg, climate change) and internal processes (e.g., urban/rural transition policies and incentives). More information about the MoST unit is available at: https://most.fbk.eu/
FBK actively seeks diversity and inclusion in the workplace and is also committed to promoting gender equality. To promote the inclusion of disabled staff as per law 68/99, the Foundation is available and interested in evaluating the applications received for technical-scientific domains that do not correspond exactly to this call.
Job Description
FBK is seeking a data scientist to support the activities of the MoST unit in the area of Social Digital Twins. The candidate will work on the analysis of geospatial and cartographic data and/or remote sensing data to extract information on urban and rural territories, such as land use and land cover, built environment and buildings, water bodies, vegetation, and surface temperature. This information will feed the digital twin models that the MoST unit develops to support public administrations, stakeholders and citizens in understanding and assessing urban and territorial transformations and policy scenarios.
These activities will be carried out within the research and innovation projects managed by the MoST unit. The candidate will work in collaboration with other FBK researchers, as well as with the partners involved in the projects.
Job requirements
The ideal candidate should have: Master's degree (or equivalent), obtained or about to be obtained, in Computer Science, Data Science, Geoinformatics, Environmental Engineering, Physics, or related fields; solid skills in data analysis, including data cleaning, integration, exploratory analysis and statistical methods; good programming skills in Python and experience with the geospatial ecosystem (e.g. GeoPandas, Rasterio, GDAL); experience in processing raster and vector data, and familiarity with GIS tools and spatial databases (e.g. QGIS, PostGIS); proficiency in English; a team working attitude; good communication and interpersonal skills; self-motivation and result orientation.
Furthermore, the following elements will be positively evaluated: experience with machine learning methods for data analysis or image classification; experience in working on research projects and/or in research groups; interest in the interplay between urban and territorial transformations and their social and policy implications.

title: A Project Manager in the field of Rural and territorial development for the Horizon Europe project TERRAE
location: Humanities and Social Sciences Hub - Trento
description:
Fondazione Bruno Kessler is a private research institution devoted to excellence in research in numerous disciplines and designated to the role of keeping the Autonomous Province of Trento in the mainstream of European and international research. Each research area is assigned to a specific research center, of which there are twelve totals. Information regarding the research centers, their activities, and production is available at http://www.fbk.eu/research-centers.
Workplace
The Digital Society (DIGIS) research center of FBK is committed to comprehensively exploring, understanding, and shaping the intricate interplay between digital technology and the fabric of human society, embracing the vision that digital technology can serve as a catalyst for positive societal change.
In particular, the Digital Society center conducts pioneering research focused on two crucial areas where ICT can have a profound impact on contemporary society: Digital Twins for Human Society to better understand, predict, and proactively address the multifaceted challenges facing them; and New Media and Education for a Resilient Society - exploring the dynamics of new media and developing advanced digital solutions towards a more inclusive, sustainable and resilient society. The center is composed of a multidisciplinary team of approximately 75 researchers, technologists and managers (including PhD students) organized in 7 research units dedicated to specific research areas in the ICT domain and 2 support units focusing on project management and technology maturation.

FBK has established the Project Management Group (PMG) to assist its research units with all of their project management needs. The PMG works across research units and administrative offices assisting and managing local, national and European projects and providing guidance and support to maximize efficiency, optimize results and reduce costs. The purpose of the PMG is to provide a unified approach for defining, managing, reporting and supporting the project management practices for the Digital Society research units. The goal of the PMG is to build and maintain transparent, predictable, and repeatable project management processes to collaborate with researchers.

FBK actively seeks diversity and inclusion in the workplace and is also committed to promoting gender equality. To promote the inclusion of disabled staff as per law 68/99, the Foundation is available and interested in evaluating the applications received for technical-scientific domains that do not correspond exactly to this call.

FBK is looking for a dynamic and highly motivated candidate to cover this position in the PMG Unit of Digital Society Center. We are looking for a Project Manager with a background in research funding programmes, EU proposal writing, grant management and project development, combined with expertise in participatory approaches, community engagement and co-design processes. The candidate will work in collaboration with other project managers of the Unit and researchers of the Digital Society and Augmented Intelligence Centers, as well as with partners involved in FBK projects, reporting directly to the Head of Unit. The candidate will work within the Horizon Europe project TERRAE - Digital Twins-Enabled Rural Resilience in Agriculture and Forestry (https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101295313) supporting the project coordination and the implementation of the local pilot on forestry, including participatory activities with local stakeholders.
Funding acquisition will also play an important role, with a good portion of time spent finding new project opportunities, writing proposals and building consortia.
The successful candidate is expected to:
Support the implementation of the Horizon Europe project TERRAE, in particular the activities connected to the management of the local pilot in Trentino, including collaboration with the Autonomous Province of Trento and set-up and coordination of participatory co-design activities with a local group of stakeholders
Provide operational support within other EU research and innovation funded projects for the design and facilitation of participatory and co-design processes involving communities and diverse stakeholder groups.
Support the participation of the DIGIS and AI centres in research and innovation programmes mainly in the areas of digital innovation, empowerment of rural and urban communities, resilient societies, green transition and disaster resilience, trustworthy and human-centric AI. Managing relations with local and international stakeholder within the scope of PMG research and innovation projects.
Reference funding programmes for this position are: Horizon Europe and Interreg (Alpine Space, Central Europe) programme, but work can extend also to other funding programmes.

title: La Fondazione Bruno Kessler ricerca un/una Cybersecurity Analyst per il Joint Lab per la Cybersecurity di FBK
description:
La Fondazione Bruno Kessler è un ente di ricerca e innovazione con sede a Trento. La Fondazione opera in una pluralità di ambiti disciplinari e mira ad ottenere risultati di eccellenza in ambito scientifico e tecnologico attraverso 2 poli scientifici, uno dedicato alle tecnologie e all’innovazione e uno alle scienze umane e sociali, organizzati in 12 Centri di ricerca. Per maggiori informazioni visita la pagina https://www.fbk.eu/it/chi-siamo/.
Il Centro per la Cybersecurity (CS) si occupa di sicurezza informatica per favorire la collaborazione tra vari stakeholder attraverso una combinazione di tecniche di gestione del rischio IT (al fine di sviluppare soluzioni di sicurezza altamente innovative che mitighino le vulnerabilità e riducano il rischio di attacchi) e tecniche di gestione della fiducia (per migliorare l'interazione tra persone e tecnologia). Nell'ambito della missione di FBK, che mira a raggiungere risultati di eccellenza scientifica e a produrre un impatto sulla società, la missione del Centro è quella di rendere queste tecniche disponibili al maggior numero di organizzazioni possibili, incluse le PMI, che rappresentano una parte sostanziale dell'economia dell'UE ma mancano di competenze in materia di cybersecurity. A tal fine, è fondamentale integrare il supporto automatizzato alla valutazione del rischio informatico con la gestione della fiducia per assistere operativamente i progettisti, gli sviluppatori e gli amministratori di soluzioni ICT nelle loro attività quotidiane.
La figura richiesta sarà inserita all'interno del Joint Lab for Cybersecurity, un hub interno condiviso tra il Centro per la Cybersecurity e il Servizio Soluzioni Digitali e Infrastrutture IT, attivo dal 1° gennaio 2025. Esso rappresenta sia una task force in caso di incidenti, sia un servizio unificato per la formazione, la consulenza ed il supporto a problemi comuni tramite soluzioni personalizzate, secondo l'approccio Zero Trust. Questo connubio si realizza a livello combinato di ricerca e produzione e deriva da competenze verticali interne nella gestione dell'identità digitale, della valutazione del rischio, della sicurezza cloud-native, della crittografia applicata e dell’amministrazione di sistemi IT complessi. Il suo obiettivo è quello di sperimentare metodi per aumentare l'incisività e la proattività nel campo della cybersecurity, ed allo stesso tempo fungere da banco di prova per la futura esportazione del modello come servizio da offrire ad altri enti provinciali ed al settore produttivo locale.
FBK promuove la diversità e l'inclusione all’interno del proprio ambiente lavorativo e sostiene la parità di genere. Al fine di promuovere l'inserimento di profili appartenenti alla Legge 68/99, la Fondazione è disponibile e interessata a valutare le candidature ricevute anche per figure professionali non corrispondenti esattamente al presente bando.
Job description

Siamo alla ricerca di persone appassionate al mondo della Cybersecurity, con spiccata curiosità intellettuale e forte attitudine all’apprendimento continuo. Cerchiamo candidati che valorizzino il lavoro di squadra, aperti al confronto e determinati nel raggiungere i propri obiettivi. Apprezziamo particolarmente un approccio proattivo alla risoluzione dei problemi, la capacità di sperimentare e di individuare soluzioni innovative, non solo in ambito di sicurezza informatica.
Il profilo ricercato avrà il compito di: Fornire supporto operativo al gruppo dedicato alla gestione del Risk Assessment dell'infrastruttura di FBK; Collaborare al monitoraggio e alla gestione dei log di sicurezza e delle identità tramite strumenti CIEM (Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management); Supportare l'analisi dei privilegi di accesso e l'applicazione delle policy di sicurezza sulle infrastrutture critiche; Identificare e segnalare eventuali anomalie, vulnerabilità o accessi non autorizzati; Creare, aggiornare e mantenere la documentazione tecnica relativa all'analisi dei rischi e alla conformità di sicurezza; Collaborare con gli altri membri del Centro di Cybersecurity per la risoluzione di problematiche complesse; Gestire i ticket di analisi di sicurezza e supporto garantendo la lavorazione entro i tempi stabiliti; Applicare e promuovere le policy aziendali sulla sicurezza informatica e la protezione dei dati. Rappresentare il team attraverso attività di formazione e divulgazione sui temi della sicurezza informatica.
La partecipazione alla procedura di selezione è subordinata al possesso del requisito di onorabilità e affidabilità, consistente nell’assenza di condanne penali definitive e di procedimenti penali pendenti che possano incidere, in ragione della loro natura, sulla valutazione dell’idoneità allo svolgimento dell’incarico di Amministratore di Sistema, con specifico riguardo alla sicurezza delle informazioni e all’accesso a sistemi e risorse critiche.
I/le candidati/e devono possedere i seguenti requisiti: Madrelingua o C1 in italiano ed ottima conoscenza della lingua inglese, sia scritta che parlata (B2 o superiore), per interagire con fornitori e utenti internazionali.
Oltre ai requisiti sopra indicati, i/le candidati/e ideali presentano le seguenti caratteristiche: Titolo di studio quinquennale ad indirizzo tecnico informatico ; Laurea triennale in informatica, ingegneria informatica, cybersecurity o discipline scientifiche affini; Esperienza pregressa in ruoli di analisi del rischio, cyber defense o supporto alla sicurezza informatica in ambienti strutturati; Buona conoscenza dei principi base di Cybersecurity, gestione delle identità e analisi del rischio; Buona conoscenza dei principali sistemi operativi (Windows, Linux, MacOS); Familiarità di base con l'analisi dei log di sistema, di rete e degli eventi di sicurezza; Buone capacità di comunicazione, public speaking e gestione delle relazioni interpersonali; Capacità di ascolto e di comprensione delle esigenze e delle architetture aziendali; Mindset proattivo, appassionato ed orientato a sperimentare e fare ricerca nell'ambito della sicurezza informatica; Pensiero analitico e critico, con capacità di analizzare problemi complessi; Spirito d'iniziativa e disponibilità all’aggiornamento continuo delle conoscenze.
Costituiscono titolo preferenziale: Esperienza nell’utilizzo di strumenti VCS (GitLab, GitHub) e linguaggi di scripting per l'automazione della sicurezza (Bash, Python, PowerShell); Conoscenza dei protocolli di rete (TCP/IP, HTTP, HTTPS, DNS, DHCP) e delle architetture di rete orientate alla sicurezza; Dimostrata capacità di utilizzo di sistemi di ticketing, SIEM o strumenti di monitoraggio della sicurezza. Comprovata esperienza o forte attitudine nell'esposizione di contenuti tecnici a pubblici sia specialistici sia non tecnici (speaker in eventi, workshop o corsi di formazione).
La Fondazione prevede un percorso di formazione e affiancamento per favorire l’inserimento e lo sviluppo professionale delle persone; le posizioni all’interno del Servizio IT sono flessibili e verranno adeguate alle competenze e al percorso delle persone che verranno inserite.

title: Tecnico di laboratori per l’Unità MNF del Centro di Ricerca Sensors & Devices
description:
Il Centro Sensors and Devices di FBK, FBK-SD, si occupa principalmente di micro-nano fabbricazione in silicio, di interesse per diversi ambiti scientifico tecnologici quali la fotonica, la fotonica integrata, i sistemi elettromeccanici (MEMS-NEMS), la sensoristica di radiazione elettromagnetica (sensori di immagini, sensori singolo fotone, dalle radiofrequenze ai raggi gamma), per le biotecnologie e la medicina, per il monitoraggio ambientale e per i processi industriali. Per la realizzazione di sensori, dispositivi e sistemi, il centro utilizza e integra anche altri materiali e componenti, impiegando competenze specifiche e dedicate. Il centro copre tutta la catena del valore, dal design al sistema completo, passando per sviluppo, fabbricazione, integrazione e packaging. Recenti investimenti in infrastruttura e l’esistenza di interessi a livello locale, nazionale ed internazionale richiedono il rafforzamento dei gruppi di lavoro dedicati all’integrazione 3D di dispositivi, alle nanotecnologie e alle tecnologie quantistiche, nuovi ambiti per il paradigma “more than Moore”.
L’Unità MNF (Micro and Nano fabrication Facility) gestisce da oltre 35 anni la maggior parte dell’infrastruttura di ricerca del centro FBK-SD che comprende una camera pulita dedicata principalmente ai sensori di radiazione ed alla fotonica, una camera pulita dedicata ai sistemi elettro-meccanici ed alla sensoristica ambientale, litografie ottiche ed elettroniche, nanofabbricazione con fascio ionico, testing parametrico, una camera pulita per l’integrazione di dispositivi e sistemi.
La qualità e affidabilità dei dispositivi sviluppati in MNF dipende non solo dall’elevata professionalità dello staff, ma anche da un controllo continuo e altrettanto competente degli impianti collegati alle cleanroom, che ne garantiscono i parametri di funzionamento necessari.
L’ampliamento delle cleanroom MNF, l'incremento del numero di attrezzature e degli impianti, l’aumentare continuo di progetti e impegni con realtà di ricerca e industriali, richiede il potenziamento delle attività di microfabbricazione. A questa esigenza si riferisce la ricerca di personale in oggetto.

FBK promuove la diversità e l'inclusione nel proprio ambiente lavorativo e sostiene l'equilibrio di genere. Al fine di promuovere l'inserimento di profili appartenenti alla Legge 68/99, la Fondazione è disponibile e interessata a valutare le candidature ricevute anche per domini tecnico-scientifici non corrispondenti esattamente al presente bando.
Descrizione attività
Il tecnico di laboratorio è la figura chiave che garantisce la continuità della produzione in cleanroom. Sarà responsabile della gestione operativa degli impianti e dei flussi di lavoro. Nello specifico, la nuova risorsa sarà coinvolta nelle seguenti attività: Gestione operativa dei processi: caricare e movimentare manualmente wafer di silicio (utilizzando pinzette specifiche) all'interno delle macchine e delle cappe chimiche, seguendo rigorose procedure operative (SOP). Conduzione macchinari: avviare e monitorare i cicli di lavoro tramite software dedicato, intervenendo con capacità di problem-solving sui piccoli malfunzionamenti o disallineamenti meccanici/elettronici. Controllo Qualità (SPC): effettuare misure di controllo dei processi, inserendo i dati nel gestionale aziendale in conformita’ con la ISO 9001:2015. Manutenzione tecnica: garantire la corretta operatività degli impianti effettuando manutenzione ordinaria e supportando gli interventi di manutenzione straordinaria in caso di guasto.
Il/La candidato/a ideale possiede i seguenti requisiti: Diploma di Perito tecnico ad indirizzo elettronico, elettrotecnico o meccanico/meccatronico o titoli equivalenti; conoscenza del Pacchetto Office (principalmente Word ed Excel) per la gestione di documentazione tecnica; ottima conoscenza della lingua italiana, scritta e parlata; buone capacità organizzative e flessibilità; spiccata attitudine al lavoro di gruppo e valide capacità comunicative.
Inoltre, saranno valutati positivamente i seguenti elementi: Buona conoscenza della lingua inglese, sia scritta che parlata, per la consultazione di manuali tecnici e l’interazione con personale internazionale; orientamento al risultato, flessibilità ed indipendenza; esperienza lavorativa, anche maturata in settori diversi da quello di riferimento; esperienza pregressa in contesti di produzione industriale o laboratori tecnologici (es. semiconduttori, micromeccanica, assemblaggio componenti elettronici etc.);

title: Tenure Track position for a Technologist in Knowledge and Project Management
description:
Fondazione Bruno Kessler is a private research institution devoted to excellence in research across numerous disciplines and designed to keep the Autonomous Province of Trento at the forefront of European and international research. Each research area is assigned to a specific research center, of which there are twelve in total. Information regarding the research centers, their activities, and production is available at http://www.fbk.eu/research-centers.
Workplace Description
The Center on Sustainable Energy (SE) supports the development of devices and methods for generation, storage, and distribution of energy solutions at low environmental impact. This will be done in the perspective of energy sustainability, of systems and solutions that respect the environment and the quality of life, of solutions with a lower impact on health and on environmental pollution levels. The ground for the Center on “Sustainable Energy” is based on the Decarbonization targets, which will demand for more flexibility of the energy system, through new gas and power grids and using energy vectors and storage solutions, as enablers for the wide penetration of renewables.
Within this strategic framework, inside Fondazione Bruno Kessler, the Center for Sustainable Energy is involved in activities that maximise the impact of research and innovation in different channels of knowledge, such as communication, dissemination and exploitation. This relevance is part of an overall strategy of positioning the internal assets of the Center towards the different stakeholders in the Scientific, Industrial, Institutional domains.
FBK actively seeks diversity and inclusion in the workplace and is also committed to promoting gender equality.

Job Description

The purpose of FBK’s Tenure Track program is to offer high-level professionals the opportunity to pursue a structured career path to become tenured researchers contributing to the organisation's long-term strategy. Within this framework, FBK is seeking to fill the position with a dynamic, highly motivated, independent technologist in the field of Knowledge and Project Management.
The position will focus on the strategic development and coordinated management of research and innovation projects and research&technology infrastructures. Working closely with the Center’s leadership, research units, laboratory managers and administrative services, the selected candidate will contribute to communication, dissemination, exploitation and project management both in projects and internal activities.
The role will connect project development and funding opportunities with the effective use of research capabilities, knowledge valorisation and industrial collaboration. It will also support synergies with other research infrastructures and the Center’s participation in relevant national and European networks, programmes and strategic initiatives.

Main Tasks:
The successful candidate will work within the FBK-SE Center and her/his responsibilities will include: Develop and implement knowledge management processes to capture, organise and share research outputs, expertise and lessons learned across the Center in compliance with FBK Corruption Prevention and Transparency Unit and ISO 9001; Support the dissemination, exploitation and valorisation of research results, in collaboration with researchers, industrial partners and FBK’s technology transfer services; Support the strategic communication of the Hydrogen Hub maximizing the sharing of knowledge through different distribution channels; Maintain an updated overview of research capabilities, project results and strategic assets, facilitating their use in new proposals, collaborations and innovation activities; Promote knowledge exchange across research units and project teams, identifying synergies and opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration; Support the identification of relevant funding opportunities and help in proposal development, including partner engagement, work plans, budgets and expected impacts; Support project management in research and innovation projects in collaboration with scientific leaders and administrative services, coordinating activities, timelines, deliverables and resources, monitoring progress, risks and dependencies, and facilitating corrective actions and reporting.
Job requirements
The ideal candidate should have: Master's Degree in Political Science, Business Administration, or similar; Knowledge Management: Proven experience in organising and sharing research knowledge, mapping expertise and results, and supporting their reuse and valorisation across projects and teams; Project Management and Monitoring: Demonstrated ability to support scientific leaders in planning and implementing research and innovation projects, monitoring deliverables, timelines, budgets and risks, and coordinating reporting with administrative services; Funding and Partnership Development: Experience in identifying national and European funding opportunities, contributing to proposal preparation, and engaging research, industrial and institutional partners; Oral and written proficiency in English (at least level B2); Self-motivation and result orientation; Teamwork approach, good communication and relational skills; Strong interpersonal skills with a track record of building collaborative relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Furthermore, the following elements will be positively evaluated: Certifications in Project Management.
Employment

Type of contract: Tenure Track position leading to an FBK 3rd Level Technologist (T3) permanent contract.
Duration: The duration of the Tenure Track contract will be determined by the Committee based on the assigned KPIs (at least one year, which may be reduced in accordance with the Committee's assessment of the candidate's abilities and skills). If the final assessment of the Tenure Track experience is positive, the selected candidate for the tenure track position will be offered a permanent T3 contract.
Working hours: full-time (38 h per week).
Gross annual salary: €47.182,01 (plus objectives achievement bonus).
Start date: December 2026
Workplace: Povo, Trento (Italy) and Rovereto
Benefits: flexi-time, company subsidised cafeteria or meal vouchers, internal car park, welcome office support for visa formalities, accommodation, supplementary pension and health found, training courses, public transport, sports facilities, language courses fees. Further details at https://www.fbk.eu/en/work-with-us/.

The Bruno Kessler Foundation invests in people’s growth and promotes a stimulating environment that values talent. Through the Talent Development Program, each participant will be engaged in a tailored experiential journey designed to enhance skills, attitudes, and aspirations. In line with this commitment, we offer a structured Research Impact and Innovation career path specifically designed for this tenure-track position. This journey provides concrete tools for professional growth, including personalized assessments to develop individual potential and a clear evolutionary roadmap that supports the transition from independent research to scientific leadership. Within our dynamic and innovative environment, development strategies are integrated with the researcher's path to help shape the future, ensuring that academic autonomy is always paired with institutional support and opportunities for international impact.
